info.title: sqlarchive
info.description: Export a SQL Server database to a readable archive, restore it somewhere else, and prove the two match.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Read a database into an archive: the schema, the rows, and a hash of each table.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --source
options.description:
Connection string of the database to
archive

options.name: --out
options.description:
The archive to write. The conventional
extension is .sqlarchive; it is not
enforced

options.name: --table
options.description:
Archive only tables matching this glob, as
schema.table. Repeatable. Default: every
table

options.name: --exclude
options.description:
Leave out tables matching this glob, as
schema.table. Repeatable. Applied after

options.name: --where
options.description:
Archive only the rows of one table that
match a predicate, as dbo.Order=Total>0.
Repeatable. The predicate is written into
the manifest as that table's rowFilter,
because an archive that is partial and does
not say so makes a later verify report
differences that are not differences

options.name: --schema-only
options.description:
Archive the schema and none of the rows.
Every table is marked dataSkipped in the
manifest, so a verify against the archive
knows the rows are absent on purpose

options.name: --consistent
options.description:
Read every table at one point in time.
Tries a database snapshot first, then a
single connection under SNAPSHOT isolation.
If neither is available it REFUSES and says
which permission or setting is missing - it
does not quietly fall back to reading table
by table, because an archive that was asked
to be consistent and silently is not is
worse than a failed export. The mode that
was used is recorded in the manifest

options.name: --maxdop
options.description:
How many units are read at once - a table
read whole is one unit, and each range of a
table that was split into ranges is one
more, so a single large table can use every
bit of this and not just one slot of it.
Default: the processor count, capped at 8.
A database snapshot keeps this parallelism;
SNAPSHOT isolation costs it, because it
reads through a single connection

options.name: --range-size
options.description:
Split a large table into range files of
about this many rows, which is what lets it
be read in parallel. Only possible where
there is a numeric or date key to partition
by; a table without one is read whole
whatever this says

options.name: --spool
options.description:
Where the partial export is spooled.
Default: beside --out

options.name: --resume
options.description:
Carry on an export that was interrupted,
doing the tables that are missing. The
spool carries a fingerprint of the
connection, the filters and the format
version; resuming with different ones is
refused rather than mixed into one archive
that came from two different runs

commands.name: import
commands.description:
Restore an archive, as a migration over what is already there rather than as a
drop.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --destination
options.description:
Connection string of the database to
restore into. It does not have to be
empty, and it does not have to be new

options.name: --schema-only
options.description:
Run the schema phases and stop. No rows
are read out of the archive

options.name: --data-only
options.description:
Skip the schema and publish the rows into
a destination that already has the right
shape. Refused where the shape does not
match

options.name: --table
options.description:
Publish the rows of only the tables
matching this glob, as schema.table.
Repeatable. It selects ROWS and not
schema: the archive's schema phases are
its own files, run whole, so a table left
out here is still created - and left
empty. The summary says which and why

options.name: --exclude
options.description:
Leave the rows of tables matching this
glob unpublished, as schema.table.
Repeatable. Applied after --table

options.name: --dry-run
options.description:
Say what would be altered and what would
be published, and write nothing. The
schema diff is real; the destination is
not touched

options.name: --continue-on-error
options.description:
Carry on with the remaining tables when
one fails. Each table is published
atomically by itself, so the ones that
succeeded stay published and the ones that
failed are left untouched - not half
loaded

options.name: --maxdop
options.description:
How many tables to stage at once. Default:
the processor count

options.name: --resume
options.description:
Carry on an interrupted restore by the
tables that are missing, against the same
fingerprint the export writes

options.name: --work-dir
options.description:
Where the journal that makes --resume
possible is kept. Default: beside the
archive. It holds no rows - the rows are
already in the archive - only which tables
are done, so a resume can pick up without
reading them again

commands.name: inspect
commands.description: Show what an archive says about itself, without unpacking it.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --entries
options.description:
List every entry with its packed and unpacked size, and
whether the manifest accounts for it

options.name: --json
options.description:
Write the manifest to standard output exactly as it is in
the archive, and nothing else. This is the way to get the
hashes in full

arguments.name: ARCHIVE
arguments.description:
The archive to read: a .sqlarchive file, an archive dbdumper
wrote, a directory holding a manifest.json, or a manifest.json
by itself

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Prove an archive is intact, or that a database still matches it down to the row.

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information

options.name: --against
options.description:
Compare the archive against a live database:
the schema by diff, and per table the row
count and the content hash. Without it, only
the integrity of the archive itself is checked
- the file hashes in the manifest against the
entries - and no server is touched at all

options.name: --table
options.description:
Verify only tables matching this glob, as
schema.table. Repeatable

options.name: --exclude
options.description:
Leave out tables matching this glob, as
schema.table. Repeatable. Applied after

options.name: --schema-only
options.description:
Compare the schema and stop. No table is read
on either side
console. A build branching on the exit code
found differences, and 1 when it could not be
a job that treats a corrupt archive and an
unreachable server as the same event will
eventually act on the wrong one

options.name: --json
options.description:
Write the verdict as JSON as well, for a build
to read. The readable report still goes to the
console. A build branching on the exit code
gets three answers rather than two: 0 when the
two sides match, 3 when the comparison ran and
found differences, and 1 when it could not be
made at all. Finding drift is not failing, and
a job that treats a corrupt archive and an
unreachable server as the same event will
eventually act on the wrong one

options.name: --maxdop
options.description:
How many tables to read at once. Default: the
processor count

options.name: --timeout
options.description:
Command timeout for reading a table. 0, the
default, is no limit: verify reads whole
tables and a clock is the wrong way to notice
a slow one

arguments.name: ARCHIVE
arguments.description:
The archive to verify, and the side of the comparison that is a
file

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints help information

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints version information
